title: Make parallel lifecycle projections merge-safe
outOfScope: Rewriting or reviving the historical projection-isolation-664 archive and stale branch.
Enabling #659 parallel starts before this corrective Work Item is merged.
Weakening fail-closed handling of unknown or shared generated projections.

sources.reason: Authoritative problem statement, dependency, and acceptance criteria.
Parallel-start dependency that must remain blocked until this correction is merged.
Existing projection-isolation regression surface and linked-worktree fixtures.

riskAssessment.reason: Branch-integrated generated facts can conflict across linked Work Items; the corrective must serialize or namespace every such projection while preserving fail-closed behavior.

reasons: Initial Work Item skeleton defaults to Standard until scope is classified.

executionDecision.reason: The user authorized automatic governed execution and requires formal corrective Work Items instead of temporary process patches.

preReviewWarnings: Two allowed Work Items must merge without conflicting branch-integrated generated projections.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: Every generated path emitted by ai-start, ai-finish, and archive is inventoried and classified as task/worktree-namespaced, non-committed, or executable serialized ownership.
Unknown or shared generated projections fail closed and cannot be omitted from the ownership boundary.
Two allowed linked Work Items can be integrated sequentially without generated-projection conflicts at merge level.
The corrected generated-projection model is consumed by the #659 parallel-start gate only after this Work Item merges.
guidelines: Keep the projection inventory executable rather than relying on a prose-only path list.
Preserve task isolation and fail closed for unclassified branch-integrated projections.
Use linked-worktree and merge-level regressions, not only unit-level locking tests.
Document the lifecycle ownership boundary and preserve the stale predecessor as audit evidence.

intent.problem: Linked worktrees isolate physical files but not branch-integrated lifecycle facts, so status, task reports, and archive index can conflict when allowed Work Items are merged.
constraints: Preserve the historical projection-isolation-664 archive and stale branch as immutable audit evidence.
Do not enable #659 parallel-start completion before this corrective merges.
Do not use manual profile downgrades, temporary patches, or implicit shared ownership.
Keep unknown or shared generated projections fail closed.
intent.rationale: An executable generated-projection ownership model plus real linked-worktree merge regression makes permitted parallel lifecycle work verifiable rather than merely plausible.
